<div class="grid-wrapper guides-configuration-reference">
  <div class="width-12-12">
    <div>
      <h1 class="text-caps">All configuration options </h1>
<div class="paragraph configuration-legend">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> Configuration property fixed at build time - All other configuration properties are overridable at runtime <input type="search" id="config-search-1" placeholder="FILTER CONFIGURATION" disabled></p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch configuration-reference searchable configuration-reference-all-rows">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 80%;">
<col style="width: 10%;">
<col style="width: 10%;">
</colgroup>
<tbody>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><span class="extension-name">Aesh</span></p></th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">Type</p></th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">Default</p></th>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-mode"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-mode"><code>quarkus.aesh.mode</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.mode' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-1" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The execution mode for the Aesh extension.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><code>auto</code> - Automatically detect the mode based on annotations. Uses runtime mode for single command or group commands, console mode for multiple commands.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>runtime</code> - Use AeshRuntimeRunner for single command execution (like picocli).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><code>console</code> - Use AeshConsoleRunner for interactive shell mode.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-1">QUARKUS_AESH_MODE</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-1" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><code>auto</code>, <code>runtime</code>, <code>console</code></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>auto</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-start-console"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-start-console"><code>quarkus.aesh.start-console</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.start-console' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-2" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether to start the local console (stdin/stdout) for interactive CLI access.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When not set, auto-detected: the local console is started if no remote transport (SSH, WebSocket) is present, and skipped if a remote transport is present.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Set to <code>true</code> to force starting the local console alongside remote transports. Set to <code>false</code> to disable the local console even without remote transports (useful when embedding commands in a server application).</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When running in dev mode with the local console enabled, set <code>quarkus.console.enabled=false</code> in <code>application.properties</code> to prevent the Quarkus dev console from competing for stdin.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-2">QUARKUS_AESH_START_CONSOLE</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-2" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">boolean</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-top-command"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-top-command"><code>quarkus.aesh.top-command</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.top-command' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-3" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Fully qualified class name of the top command to use in runtime mode. or FQCN of class which will be used as entry point for Aesh CommandRunner instance. This class needs to be annotated with <code>org.aesh.command.Command</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-3">QUARKUS_AESH_TOP_COMMAND</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-3" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">string</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-prompt"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-prompt"><code>quarkus.aesh.prompt</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.prompt' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-4" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The prompt to display in console mode. Only used when mode is set to 'console' or auto-detected as console.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-4">QUARKUS_AESH_PROMPT</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-4" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">string</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>[quarkus]$ </code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-add-exit-command"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-add-exit-command"><code>quarkus.aesh.add-exit-command</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.add-exit-command' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-5" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether to add a built-in 'exit' command in console mode. Only used when mode is set to 'console' or auto-detected as console.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-5">QUARKUS_AESH_ADD_EXIT_COMMAND</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-5" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">boolean</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>true</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-enable-alias"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-enable-alias"><code>quarkus.aesh.enable-alias</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.enable-alias' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-6" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Enable command aliasing. When enabled, users can create aliases for commands.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-6">QUARKUS_AESH_ENABLE_ALIAS</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-6" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">boolean</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>false</code></p></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-enable-export"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-enable-export"><code>quarkus.aesh.enable-export</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.enable-export' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-7" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Enable the export command. When enabled, the 'export' command is available for setting environment variables.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-7">QUARKUS_AESH_ENABLE_EXPORT</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-7" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">

</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-enable-man"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-aesh_quarkus-aesh-enable-man"><code>quarkus.aesh.enable-man</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.aesh.enable-man' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-8" class="openblock description description-collapsed">

</div>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-24" class="openblock description description-collapsed">

<div class="paragraph">
<p>For production, use public key authentication via <code>authorized-keys-file</code> instead. If password authentication is needed, avoid storing the password in plaintext in <code>application.properties</code>. Instead, reference an environment variable:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="highlightjs highlight"><code class="language-none hljs">quarkus.aesh.ssh.password=${SSH_PASSWORD}</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-24">QUARKUS_AESH_SSH_PASSWORD</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-24" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>

<p><a id="quarkus-agroal_quarkus-datasource-jdbc-enable-recovery"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-agroal_quarkus-datasource-jdbc-enable-recovery"><code>quarkus.datasource.jdbc.enable-recovery</code></a></span>

</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-65" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether to enable recovery for this datasource.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Normally a transaction manager will call xa_recover () on an XA connection during recovery to obtain a list of transaction branches that are currently in a prepared or heuristically completed state. However, it can happen that multiple XA connections connect to the same datasource which would all return the same set of branches and for reasons of improved performance only one should be used for recover() calls. The default value for this configuration property is true because when there is only one connection it is vital for data consistency that the connection is able to report its list of prepared or heuristically completed branches.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-65">QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_JDBC_ENABLE_RECOVERY</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-65" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

</div>

<li>
<p>If set to <code>all</code> (or <code>true</code>) the container will attempt to remove all unused beans.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If set to <code>none</code> (or <code>false</code>) no beans will ever be removed even if they are unused (according to the criteria set out below)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>If set to <code>fwk</code>, then all unused beans will be removed, except the unused beans whose classes are declared in the application code</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An unused bean:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>is not a built-in bean or interceptor,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>is not eligible for injection to any injection point,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>is not excluded by any extension,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>does not have a name,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>does not declare an observer,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>does not declare any producer which is eligible for injection to any injection point,</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>is not directly eligible for injection into any <code>jakarta.enterprise.inject.Instance</code> injection point</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-89">QUARKUS_ARC_REMOVE_UNUSED_BEANS</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-89" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">string</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>all</code></p></td>
</tr>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-91" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If set to true, the bytecode of unproxyable beans will be transformed. This ensures that a proxy/subclass can be created properly. If the value is set to false, then an exception is thrown at build time indicating that a subclass/proxy could not be created. Quarkus performs the following transformations when this setting is enabled:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Remove 'final' modifier from classes and methods when a proxy is required.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Create a no-args constructor if needed.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Makes private no-args constructors package-private if necessary.</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>

<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.arc.detect-wrong-annotations' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-103" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If set to true then the container attempts to detect <em>wrong</em> usages of annotations and eventually fails the build to prevent unexpected behavior of a Quarkus application.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A typical example is <code>@jakarta.ejb.Singleton</code> which is often confused with <code>@jakarta.inject.Singleton</code>. As a result a component annotated with <code>@jakarta.ejb.Singleton</code> would be completely ignored. Another example is an inner class annotated with a scope annotation - this component would be again completely ignored.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-103">QUARKUS_ARC_DETECT_WRONG_ANNOTATIONS</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-103" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-arc_quarkus-arc-strict-compatibility"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-arc_quarkus-arc-strict-compatibility"><code>quarkus.arc.strict-compatibility</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.arc.strict-compatibility' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-104" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If set to <code>true</code>, the container will perform additional validations mandated by the CDI specification. Some improvements on top of the CDI specification may be disabled. Applications that work as expected in the strict mode should work without a change in the default, non-strict mode.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The strict mode is mainly introduced to allow passing the CDI Lite TCK. Applications are recommended to use the default, non-strict mode, which makes CDI more convenient to use. The "strictness" of the strict mode (the set of additional validations and the set of disabled improvements on top of the CDI specification) may change over time.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Note that <code>transform-unproxyable-classes</code> and <code>remove-unused-beans</code> also has effect on specification compatibility. You may want to disable these features to get behavior closer to the specification.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-104">QUARKUS_ARC_STRICT_COMPATIBILITY</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-104" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Classes generated by Avro (annotated with <code>@org.apache.avro.specific.AvroGenerated</code>) are always trusted and do not need to be listed here.</p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-121" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Description of each type can be found <a href="https://github.com/microsoft/azure-maven-plugins/wiki/Authentication">here</a> Valid values are</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>azure_cli</strong> Delegates to Azure CLI for login</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>managed_identity</strong> Requires client to be set</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>oauth2</strong> Requires tenant to be set</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>device_code</strong> Requires tenant to be set</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>file</strong> Filesystem path to a property file that defines authentication. Properties supported are</p>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>type</strong> Supports same type values as well as <em>service_principal</em></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>client</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>tenant</strong></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>key</strong> Password for <em>service_principal</em> if using password authentication</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>certificate</strong> Path to PEM file if using <em>service_principal</em></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>certificate-password</strong> Password for PEM file if it is password protected and if using <em>service_principal</em></p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>environment</strong> if using <em>service_principal</em></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Defaults to "azure_cli" for authentication</p>

<div class="paragraph">

<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><span class="extension-name">Container Image - Jib</span></p></th>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-187" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The base image to be used when a container image is being produced for the jar build. When the application is built against Java 25 or higher, <code>registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-25-runtime:1.24</code> is used as the default. Otherwise, when the application is built against Java 21 to Java 24, <code>registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-21-runtime:1.24</code> is used as the default. Otherwise <code>registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-17-runtime:1.24</code> is used as the default.</p>
</div>

<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-container-image-jib_quarkus-jib-jvm-entrypoint"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-container-image-jib_quarkus-jib-jvm-entrypoint"><code>quarkus.jib.jvm-entrypoint</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.jib.jvm-entrypoint' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-192" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If this is set, then it will be used as the entry point of the container image. There are a few things to be aware of when creating an entry point</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>Entrypoint "INHERIT" means to inherit entrypoint from base image, <code>jvmArguments</code> field is used for arguments</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>A valid entrypoint is jar package specific (see <code>quarkus.package.jar.type</code>)</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>A valid entrypoint depends on the location of both the launching scripts and the application jar file. To that end it&#8217;s helpful to remember that when <code>fast-jar</code> packaging is used (the default), all necessary application jars are added to the <code>/work</code> directory and that the same directory is also used as the working directory. When <code>legacy-jar</code> or <code>uber-jar</code> are used, the application jars are unpacked under the <code>/app</code> directory and that directory is used as the working directory.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Even if the <code>jvmArguments</code> field is set, it is ignored completely unless entrypoint is "INHERIT"</p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When this is not set, a proper default entrypoint will be constructed. As a final note, a very useful tool for inspecting container image layers that can greatly aid when debugging problems with endpoints is <a href="https://github.com/wagoodman/dive">dive</a></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-192">QUARKUS_JIB_JVM_ENTRYPOINT</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-192" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-container-image-jib_quarkus-jib-platforms"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-container-image-jib_quarkus-jib-platforms"><code>quarkus.jib.platforms</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.jib.platforms' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-201" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>List of target platforms. Each platform is defined using the pattern:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="highlightjs highlight"><code class="language-none hljs">&lt;os&gt;|&lt;arch&gt;[/variant]|&lt;os&gt;/&lt;arch&gt;[/variant]</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>for example:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="highlightjs highlight"><code class="language-none hljs">linux/amd64,linux/arm64/v8</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If not specified, OS default is linux and architecture default is <code>amd64</code>. If more than one platform is configured, it is important to note that the base image has to be a Docker manifest or an OCI image index containing a version of each chosen platform. The feature does not work with native images, as cross-compilation is not supported. This configuration is based on an incubating feature of Jib. See <a href="https://github.com/GoogleContainerTools/jib/blob/master/docs/faq.md#how-do-i-specify-a-platform-in-the-manifest-list-or-oci-index-of-a-base-image">Jib FAQ</a> for more information.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-201">QUARKUS_JIB_PLATFORMS</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-201" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>

<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-container-image-jib_quarkus-jib-use-current-timestamp-file-modification"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-container-image-jib_quarkus-jib-use-current-timestamp-file-modification"><code>quarkus.jib.use-current-timestamp-file-modification</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.jib.use-current-timestamp-file-modification' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-208" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether to set the modification time (last modified time) of the files put by Jib in the image to the actual build time. Otherwise, the modification time will be set to the Unix epoch (00:00:00, January 1st, 1970 in UTC). If the modification time is constant (flag is set to false so Unix epoch is used) across two consecutive builds, the docker layer sha256 digest will be different only if the actual files added by Jib to the docker layer were changed. More exactly, having 2 consecutive builds will generate different docker layers only if the actual content of the files within the docker layer was changed. If the current timestamp is used the sha256 digest of the docker layer will always be different even if the content of the files didn&#8217;t change.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-208">QUARKUS_JIB_USE_CURRENT_TIMESTAMP_FILE_MODIFICATION</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-208" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>

<p>The base image to be used when a container image is being produced for the jar build. The value of this property is used to create an ImageStream for the builder image used in the OpenShift build. When the application is built against Java 25 or higher, <code>registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-25:1.24</code> is used as the default. Otherwise, when the application is built against Java 21 to Java 24, <code>registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-21:1.24</code> is used as the default. Otherwise <code>registry.access.redhat.com/ubi9/openjdk-17:1.24</code> is used as the default.</p>

</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-245" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, the bootstrap mechanism will create a shared cache of open JARs for Quarkus classloaders to reduce the total number of opened ZIP FileSystems in dev and test modes. Setting system property <code>quarkus.bootstrap.disable-jar-cache</code> to <code>true</code> will make Quarkus classloaders create a new ZIP FileSystem for each JAR classpath element every time it is added to a Quarkus classloader.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">

<p>When running in dev and test mode these resources are hidden from the ClassLoader, when running in production mode these files are removed from the jars that contain them.</p>

<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-core_quarkus-config-fixed-at-build-time"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-core_quarkus-config-fixed-at-build-time"><code>quarkus.config.fixed-at-build-time</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.config.fixed-at-build-time' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-275" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If set to <code>true</code>, all configuration is frozen at build time. All values from <code>application.properties</code> and similar file-based sources are baked into the application artifact at the highest priority. At runtime, no external configuration sources are consulted: no <code>application.properties</code>, no <code>.env</code> files, no system properties, and no environment variables can affect configuration values.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The only exceptions are a small set of JVM environment properties (<code>java.io.tmpdir</code>, <code>user.home</code>, <code>user.dir</code>) which are resolved at runtime to support <code>@WithDefault</code> expressions whose values are inherently machine-dependent.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This is useful for CLI applications and sealed/immutable deployments where the binary&#8217;s behavior must be fully determined at build time.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Computed defaults (<code>@WithDefault</code>) and programmatic values set by recorders still work normally. When enabled, this supersedes <code>quarkus.config.sources.system-only</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-275">QUARKUS_CONFIG_FIXED_AT_BUILD_TIME</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-275" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">boolean</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>false</code></p></td>
</tr>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-304" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Detection mode of invalid usage of execution model annotations.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An execution model annotation is <code>@Blocking</code>, <code>@NonBlocking</code> and <code>@RunOnVirtualThread</code>. These annotations may only be used on "entrypoint" methods (methods invoked by various frameworks in Quarkus); using them on methods that can only be invoked by application code is invalid.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-304">QUARKUS_EXECUTION_MODEL_ANNOTATIONS_DETECTION_MODE</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-304" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-323" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The set of supported locales that can be consumed by the extensions.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The locales must be specified in the IETF BCP 47 format e.g. en-US or fr-FR.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For instance, the Hibernate Validator extension makes use of it.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Native-image build uses it to define additional locales that are supposed to be available at runtime.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A special string "all" is translated as ROOT Locale and then used in native-image to include all locales. Image size penalty applies.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-323">QUARKUS_LOCALES</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-323" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-324" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Default locale that can be consumed by the extensions.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The locale must be specified in the IETF BCP 47 format e.g. en-US or fr-FR.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For instance, the Hibernate Validator extension makes use of it.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Native-image build uses this property to derive <code>user.language</code> and <code>user.country</code> for the application&#8217;s runtime. Starting with GraalVM for JDK 24 <code>user.language</code> and <code>user.country</code> can also be overridden at runtime, provided the selected locale was included at image build time.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">

</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As an example, to get <code>TRACE</code> logging, minimum level needs to be at <code>TRACE</code>, and the runtime log level needs to match that.</p>

<div class="paragraph">
<p>The maximum log file size, after which a rotation is executed, up to <code>Long.MAX_VALUE</code> bytes. Note that the file is rotated <em>after</em> the log record is written. Thus, this isn&#8217;t a hard maximum on the file size; rather, it&#8217;s a hard <em>minimum</em> on the size of the file before it is rotated.</p>

<div class="paragraph">

</div>
<div class="paragraph">

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-463" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The strategy for pulling the builder image during the build.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Defaults to 'always', which will always pull the most up-to-date image; useful to keep up with fixes when a (floating) tag is updated.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Use 'missing' to only pull if there is no image locally; useful on development environments where building with out-of-date images is acceptable and bandwidth may be limited.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Use 'never' to fail the build if there is no image locally.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">

<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-core_quarkus-native-reuse-existing"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-core_quarkus-native-reuse-existing"><code>quarkus.native.reuse-existing</code></a></span>

</div></div></td>

<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>false</code></p></td>

<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-core_quarkus-native-resources-includes"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-core_quarkus-native-resources-includes"><code>quarkus.native.resources.includes</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.native.resources.includes' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-472" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A comma separated list of globs to match resource paths that should be added to the native image.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Use slash (<code>/</code>) as a path separator on all platforms. Globs must not start with slash.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, no resources are included.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Example: Given that you have <code>src/main/resources/ignored.png</code> and <code>src/main/resources/foo/selected.png</code> in your source tree and one of your dependency JARs contains <code>bar/some.txt</code> file, with the following configuration</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="highlightjs highlight"><code class="language-none hljs">quarkus.native.resources.includes = foo/**,bar/**/*.txt</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>the files <code>src/main/resources/foo/selected.png</code> and <code>bar/some.txt</code> will be included in the native image, while <code>src/main/resources/ignored.png</code> will not be included.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Supported glob features</p>
</div>
<table class="tableblock frame-all grid-all stretch">
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%;">
<col style="width: 50%;">
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Feature</th>
<th class="tableblock halign-left valign-top">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>*</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches a (possibly empty) sequence of characters that does not contain slash (<code>/</code>)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>**</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches a (possibly empty) sequence of characters that may contain slash (<code>/</code>)</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>?</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches one character, but not slash</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>[abc]</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches one character given in the bracket, but not slash</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>[a-z]</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches one character from the range given in the bracket, but not slash</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>[!abc]</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches one character not named in the bracket; does not match slash</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>[a-z]</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches one character outside the range given in the bracket; does not match slash</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>{one,two,three}</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">Matches any of the alternating tokens separated by comma; the tokens may contain wildcards, nested alternations and ranges</p></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock"><code>\</code></p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><p class="tableblock">The escape character</p></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Note that there are three levels of escaping when passing this option via <code>application.properties</code>:</p>
</div>
<div class="olist arabic">
<ol class="arabic">
<li>
<p><code>application.properties</code> parser</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>MicroProfile Config list converter that splits the comma separated list</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Glob parser</p>
</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>All three levels use backslash (<code>\</code>) as the escaping character. So you need to use an appropriate number of backslashes depending on which level you want to escape.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Note that Quarkus extensions typically include the resources they require by themselves. This option is useful in situations when the built-in functionality is not sufficient.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-472">QUARKUS_NATIVE_RESOURCES_INCLUDES</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-472" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">list of string</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-core_quarkus-native-resources-excludes"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-core_quarkus-native-resources-excludes"><span class="line-through"><code>quarkus.native.resources.excludes</code></span></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.native.resources.excludes' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-473" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p><em>This property is deprecated since <code>3.29</code>: Excluding resources is not supported in the new reachability-metadata.json file used with Mandrel/GraalVM 25.0 and onwards. Quarkus plans to adopt the use of reachability-metadata.json for Mandrel/GraalVM 23.1 for JDK 21 as well (see <a href="https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/41016" class="bare">https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/41016</a>).</em></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A comma separated list of globs to match resource paths that should <strong>not</strong> be added to the native image.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Use slash (<code>/</code>) as a path separator on all platforms. Globs must not start with slash.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Please refer to <code>includes</code> for details about the glob syntax.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, no resources are excluded.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Example: Given that you have <code>src/main/resources/red.png</code> and <code>src/main/resources/foo/green.png</code> in your source tree and one of your dependency JARs contains <code>bar/blue.png</code> file, with the following configuration</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="highlightjs highlight"><code class="language-none hljs">quarkus.native.resources.includes = **/*.png
quarkus.native.resources.excludes = foo/**,**/green.png</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>the resource <code>red.png</code> will be available in the native image while the resources <code>foo/green.png</code> and <code>bar/blue.png</code> will not be available in the native image.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-473">QUARKUS_NATIVE_RESOURCES_EXCLUDES</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-473" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-482" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Configuration files generated by the Quarkus build, using native image agent, are informative by default. In other words, the generated configuration files are presented in the build log but are not applied. When this option is set to true, generated configuration files are applied to the native executable building process.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Enabling this option should be done with care, because it can make native image configuration and/or behaviour dependant on other non-obvious factors. For example, if the native image agent generated configuration was generated from running JVM unit tests, disabling test(s) can result in a different native image configuration being generated, which in turn can misconfigure the native executable or affect its behaviour in unintended ways.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-482">QUARKUS_NATIVE_AGENT_CONFIGURATION_APPLY</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-482" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-495" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>List of all the dependencies that have been defined as optional to include into the final package of the application. Each optional dependency needs to be expressed in the following format:</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><code>groupId:artifactId[:[classifier][:[type]]]</code></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>With the classifier and type being optional (note that the brackets (<code>[]</code>) denote optionality and are not a part of the syntax specification). The group ID and artifact ID must be present and non-empty.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the type is missing, the artifact is assumed to be of type <code>jar</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This parameter is optional; if absent, no optional dependencies will be included into the final package of the application.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For backward compatibility reasons, this parameter is ignored by default and can be enabled by setting the parameter <code>quarkus.package.jar.filter-optional-dependencies</code> to <code>true</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This parameter is meant to be used in modules where multi-builds have been configured to avoid getting a final package with unused dependencies.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-495">QUARKUS_PACKAGE_JAR_INCLUDED_OPTIONAL_DEPENDENCIES</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-495" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Dependency artifacts to exclude from tree-shaking. All classes from excluded artifacts are preserved regardless of reachability analysis.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This is useful for libraries that perform self-integrity checks (e.g., BouncyCastle FIPS) or that load classes in ways the tree-shaker cannot detect.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Each dependency is expressed as <code>groupId:artifactId[:[classifier][:[type]]]</code>. The classifier and type are optional. If the type is missing, <code>jar</code> is assumed.</p>

<p>Indicates a list of dependency for which the jar will use artifactId.type filename scheme Each dependency needs to be expressed in the following format:</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><code>groupId:artifactId[:[classifier][:[type]]]</code></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>With the classifier and type being optional (note that the brackets (<code>[]</code>) denote optionality and are not a part of the syntax specification). The group ID and artifact ID must be present and non-empty.</p>

<p>If the type is missing, the artifact is assumed to be of type <code>jar</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This parameter is optional; if absent, jar names will use groupId.artifactId[-version][-classifier].type scheme Note that using this parameter is not recommended and only be used for specific corner cases when the jar name is enforced.</p>

<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-core_quarkus-package-write-transformed-bytecode-to-build-output"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-core_quarkus-package-write-transformed-bytecode-to-build-output"><code>quarkus.package.write-transformed-bytecode-to-build-output</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.package.write-transformed-bytecode-to-build-output' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-511" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Setting this switch to <code>true</code> will cause Quarkus to write the transformed application bytecode to the build tool&#8217;s output directory. This is useful for post-build tools that need to scan the application bytecode (for example, offline code-coverage tools).</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For example, if using Maven, enabling this feature will result in the classes in <code>target/classes</code> being replaced with classes that have been transformed by Quarkus.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Setting this to <code>true</code>, however, should be done with a lot of caution and only if subsequent builds are done in a clean environment (i.e. the build tool&#8217;s output directory has been completely cleaned).</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-511">QUARKUS_PACKAGE_WRITE_TRANSFORMED_BYTECODE_TO_BUILD_OUTPUT</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-511" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-518" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Delay between shutdown being requested and actually initiated. Also called the pre-shutdown phase. In pre-shutdown, the server continues working as usual, except a readiness probe starts reporting "down" (if the <code>smallrye-health</code> extension is present). This gives the infrastructure time to detect that the application instance is shutting down and stop routing traffic to it.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Notice that this property will only take effect if <code>quarkus.shutdown.delay-enabled</code> is explicitly set to <code>true</code>.</p>
</div>

</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-558" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The executor growth resistance.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A resistance factor applied after the core pool is full; values applied here will cause that fraction of submissions to create new threads when no idle thread is available. A value of <code>0.0f</code> implies that threads beyond the core size should be created as aggressively as threads within it; a value of <code>1.0f</code> implies that threads beyond the core size should never be created.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-558">QUARKUS_THREAD_POOL_GROWTH_RESISTANCE</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-558" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>

</div>

<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">float</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>0.0</code></p></td>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-574" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Controls whether the embedded SBOM is served GZIP-compressed through the <em>endpoint</em>. This option does not affect how the SBOM is stored in the application: the embedded SBOM resource is always stored uncompressed.</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>if set to <code>true</code>, the endpoint always serves the SBOM compressed with <code>Content-Encoding: gzip</code>;</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>if set to <code>false</code>, the endpoint always serves the SBOM uncompressed;</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>if not set, the endpoint negotiates the encoding based on the request&#8217;s <code>Accept-Encoding</code> header, serving the SBOM compressed only when the client accepts <code>gzip</code>.</p>
</li>
</ul>

<p><span class="icon"><i class="fa fa-lock" title="Fixed at build time"></i></span> <a id="quarkus-datasource_quarkus-datasource-db-version"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-datasource_quarkus-datasource-db-version"><code>quarkus.datasource.db-version</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.datasource.db-version' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p><code>quarkus.datasource."datasource-name".db-version</code>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.datasource."datasource-name".db-version' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-580" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The version of the database we will connect to (e.g. '10.0').</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock caution">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-caution" title="Caution"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
The version number set here should follow the same numbering scheme
as the string returned by <code>java.sql.DatabaseMetaData#getDatabaseProductVersion()</code>
for your database&#8217;s JDBC driver.
This numbering scheme may be different from the most popular one for your database;
for example Microsoft SQL Server 2016 would be version <code>13</code>,
and Oracle Database 26ai would be version <code>23.26</code>.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As a rule, the version set here should be as high as possible,
but must be lower than or equal to the version of any database your application will connect to.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>A high version will allow better performance and using more features
(e.g. Hibernate ORM may generate more efficient SQL,
avoid workarounds and take advantage of more database features),
but if it is higher than the version of the database you want to connect to,
it may lead to runtime exceptions
(e.g. Hibernate ORM may generate invalid SQL that your database will reject).</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Some extensions (like the Hibernate ORM extension)
will try to check this version against the actual database version on startup,
leading to a startup failure when the actual version is lower
or simply a warning in case the database cannot be reached.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The default for this property is specific to each extension;
the Hibernate ORM extension will default to the oldest version it supports.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-580">QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_DB_VERSION</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-580" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">string</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"></td>

<li>
<p>MariaDB: <code>docker.io/library/mariadb:12.1</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Microsoft SQL Server: <code>mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest</code><br>
On ARM (aarch64),<code>mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge:latest</code> is used instead, because the standard MS SQL Server image does not run on ARM.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>MySQL: <code>docker.io/library/mysql:9.5</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Oracle Express Edition: <code>docker.io/gvenzl/oracle-free:23-slim-faststart</code></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>PostgreSQL: <code>docker.io/library/postgres:18</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">

(e.g., spatial or vector support). Explicitly setting this property overrides the automatic image selection.</p>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-599" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The volumes to be mapped to the container.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The map key corresponds to the host location; the map value is the container location. If the host location starts with "classpath:", the mapping loads the resource from the classpath with read-only permission.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When using a file system location, the volume will be generated with read-write permission, potentially leading to data loss or modification in your file system.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This has no effect if the provider is not a container-based database, such as H2 or Derby.</p>
</div>

<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.datasource.devservices.reuse' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<div class="paragraph">
<p><code>quarkus.datasource."datasource-name".devservices.reuse</code>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.datasource."datasource-name".devservices.reuse' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-600" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether to keep Dev Service containers running <strong>after a dev mode session or test suite execution</strong>
to reuse them in the next dev mode session or test suite execution.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Within a dev mode session or test suite execution,
Quarkus will always reuse Dev Services as long as their configuration
(username, password, environment, port bindings, &#8230;&#8203;) did not change.
This feature is specifically about keeping containers running
<strong>when Quarkus is not running</strong> to reuse them across runs.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonitionblock warning">
<table>
<tr>
<td class="icon">
<i class="fa icon-warning" title="Warning"></i>
</td>
<td class="content">
This feature needs to be enabled explicitly in <code>testcontainers.properties</code>,
may require changes to how you configure data initialization in dev mode and tests,
and may leave containers running indefinitely, forcing you to stop and remove them manually.
See <a href="/guides/databases-dev-services/#reuse">this section of the documentation</a> for more information.
</td>
</tr>
</table>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This configuration property is set to <code>true</code> by default,
so it is mostly useful to <strong>disable</strong> reuse,
if you enabled it in <code>testcontainers.properties</code>
but only want to use it for some of your Quarkus applications or datasources.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-600">QUARKUS_DATASOURCE_DEVSERVICES_REUSE</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-600" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-605" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Determines if the Keycloak container is shared. When shared, Quarkus uses label-based service discovery to find and reuse a running Keycloak container, so a second one is not started. Otherwise, if a matching container is not is found, a new container is started. The service discovery uses the <code>quarkus-dev-service-label</code> label, whose value is set by the <code>service-name</code> property. Container sharing is available only in dev mode.</p>

<p>A common root path for non-application endpoints. Various extension-provided endpoints such as metrics, health, and openapi are deployed under this path by default.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>* Relative path (Default, <code>q</code>) &#8594; Non-application endpoints will be served from <code>${quarkus.http.root-path}/${quarkus.http.non-application-root-path}</code>. * Absolute path (<code>/q</code>) &#8594; Non-application endpoints will be served from the specified path. * <code>${quarkus.http.root-path}</code> &#8594; Setting this path to the same value as HTTP root path disables this root path. All extension-provided endpoints will be served from <code>${quarkus.http.root-path}</code>.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If the management interface is enabled, the root path for the endpoints exposed on the management interface is configured using the <code>quarkus.management.root-path</code> property instead of this property.</p>

It implies loading libbrotli native library via JNI and in case of native image, packing the native library into the native image as a resource thus inflating its size. <div class="paragraph">

</div>

<p>In dev/test mode this defaults to localhost, in prod mode this defaults to 0.0.0.0</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Defaulting to 0.0.0.0 makes it easier to deploy Quarkus to container, however it is not suitable for dev/test mode as other people on the network can connect to your development machine.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>As an exception, when running in Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL), the HTTP host defaults to 0.0.0.0 even in dev/test mode since using localhost makes the application inaccessible.</p>

If this is <code>enabled</code> then http works as normal. <code>redirect</code> will still open the http port, but all requests will be redirected to the HTTPS port. <code>disabled</code> will prevent the HTTP port from opening at all.</p>

<div class="paragraph">
<p>Default is <code>enabled</code> except when client auth is set to <code>required</code> (configured using <code>quarkus.http.ssl.client-auth=required</code>). In this case, the default is <code>disabled</code>.</p>

<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-body-handle-file-uploads"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-body-handle-file-uploads"><code>quarkus.http.body.handle-file-uploads</code></a></span>

<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-688" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether the files sent using <code>multipart/form-data</code> will be stored locally.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If <code>true</code>, they will be stored in <code>quarkus.http.body-handler.uploads-directory</code> and will be made available via <code>io.vertx.ext.web.RoutingContext.fileUploads()</code>. Otherwise, the files sent using <code>multipart/form-data</code> will not be stored locally, and <code>io.vertx.ext.web.RoutingContext.fileUploads()</code> will always return an empty collection. Note that even with this option being set to <code>false</code>, the <code>multipart/form-data</code> requests will be accepted.</p>
</div>

<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-use-semicolon-as-query-param-delimiter"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-use-semicolon-as-query-param-delimiter"><code>quarkus.http.use-semicolon-as-query-param-delimiter</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.http.use-semicolon-as-query-param-delimiter' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-699" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Whether the HTTP server should treat the semicolon (<code>;</code>) as a query parameter delimiter, in addition to the ampersand (<code>&amp;</code>).</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>When set to <code>true</code> (the default), a request like <code>/path?a=1;b=2</code> is parsed as two parameters (<code>a=1</code> and <code>b=2</code>). When set to <code>false</code>, the semicolon is treated as a literal character and the request yields a single parameter (<code>a=1;b=2</code>).</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The default is <code>true</code> to preserve backward compatibility. It will change to <code>false</code> in Quarkus 4, as using the semicolon as a query parameter delimiter is uncommon and can cause issues when semicolons appear as part of parameter values.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-699">QUARKUS_HTTP_USE_SEMICOLON_AS_QUERY_PARAM_DELIMITER</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-699" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">boolean</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>true</code></p></td>

</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden odd">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-permission-permissions-methods"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-permission-permissions-methods"><code>quarkus.http.auth.permission."permissions".methods</code></a></span>

</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-715" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The methods that this permission set applies to. If this is not set then they apply to all methods.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Note that if a request matches any path from any permission set, but does not match the constraint due to the method not being listed then the request will be denied.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Method specific permissions take precedence over matches that do not have any methods set.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This means that for example if Quarkus is configured to allow GET and POST requests to /admin to and no other permissions are configured PUT requests to /admin will be denied.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-715">QUARKUS_HTTP_AUTH_PERMISSION__PERMISSIONS__METHODS</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-715" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>

</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">list of string</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"></td>
</tr>
<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-permission-permissions-paths"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-permission-permissions-paths"><code>quarkus.http.auth.permission."permissions".paths</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.http.auth.permission."permissions".paths' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-716" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>The paths that this permission check applies to. If the path ends in /* then this is treated as a path prefix, otherwise it is treated as an exact match.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Matches are done on a length basis, so the most specific path match takes precedence.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>If multiple permission sets match the same path then explicit methods matches take precedence over matches without methods set, otherwise the most restrictive permissions are applied.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-716">QUARKUS_HTTP_AUTH_PERMISSION__PERMISSIONS__PATHS</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-716" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>

<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-certificate-role-attribute"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-certificate-role-attribute"><code>quarkus.http.auth.certificate-role-attribute</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.http.auth.certificate-role-attribute' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-725" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Client certificate attribute whose values are going to be mapped to the 'SecurityIdentity' roles according to the roles mapping specified in the certificate properties file. The attribute must be either one of the Relative Distinguished Names (RDNs) or Subject Alternative Names (SANs). By default, the Common Name (CN) attribute value is used for roles mapping. Supported values are:</p>
</div>
<div class="ulist">
<ul>
<li>
<p>RDN type - Distinguished Name field. For example 'CN' represents Common Name field. Multivalued RNDs and multiple instances of the same attributes are currently not supported.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>'SAN_RFC822' - Subject Alternative Name field RFC 822 Name.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>'SAN_URI' - Subject Alternative Name field Uniform Resource Identifier (URI).</p>
</li>
<li>
<p>'SAN_ANY' - Subject Alternative Name field Other Name. Please note that only simple case of UTF8 identifier mapping is supported. For example, you can map 'other-identifier' to the SecurityIdentity roles. If you use 'openssl' tool, supported Other name definition would look like this: <code>subjectAltName=otherName:1.2.3.4;UTF8:other-identifier</code></p>
</li>
</ul>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">

<tr class="row-collapsible row-collapsed row-with-desc row-hidden">
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-form-new-cookie-interval"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-form-new-cookie-interval"><code>quarkus.http.auth.form.new-cookie-interval</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.http.auth.form.new-cookie-interval' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-738" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>How old a cookie can get before it will be replaced with a new cookie with an updated timeout, also referred to as "renewal-timeout".</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Note that smaller values will result in slightly more server load (as new encrypted cookies will be generated more often); however, larger values affect the inactivity timeout because the timeout is set when a cookie is generated.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>For example if this is set to 10 minutes, and the inactivity timeout is 30m, if a user&#8217;s last request is when the cookie is 9m old then the actual timeout will happen 21m after the last request because the timeout is only refreshed when a new cookie is generated.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>That is, no timeout is tracked on the server side; the timestamp is encoded and encrypted in the cookie itself, and it is decrypted and parsed with each request.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-738">QUARKUS_HTTP_AUTH_FORM_NEW_COOKIE_INTERVAL</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-738" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>

<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>1M</code></p></td>

<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-top"><div class="content"><div class="paragraph">
<p><a id="quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-inclusive"></a> <span class="property-path"><a href="#quarkus-vertx-http_quarkus-http-auth-inclusive"><code>quarkus.http.auth.inclusive</code></a></span>
<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.http.auth.inclusive' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
<div id="conf-collapsible-desc-747" class="openblock description description-collapsed">
<div class="content">
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Require that all registered HTTP authentication mechanisms must attempt to verify the request credentials.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>By default, when the <code>inclusive-mode</code> is strict, every registered authentication mechanism must produce SecurityIdentity, otherwise, a number of mechanisms which produce the identity may be less than a total number of registered mechanisms.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>All produced security identities can be retrieved using the following utility method:</p>
</div>
<div class="listingblock">
<div class="content">
<pre class="highlightjs highlight"><code class="language-none hljs">`io.quarkus.vertx.http.runtime.security.HttpSecurityUtils++#++getSecurityIdentities(io.quarkus.security.identity.SecurityIdentity)`</code></pre>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>An injected <code>SecurityIdentity</code> represents an identity produced by the first inclusive authentication mechanism. When the <code>mTLS</code> authentication is required, the <code>mTLS</code> mechanism is always the first mechanism, because its priority is elevated when inclusive authentication</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This property is false by default which means that the authentication process is complete as soon as the first <code>SecurityIdentity</code> is created.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>This property will be ignored if the path specific authentication is enabled.</p>
</div>
<div class="paragraph">
<p>Environment variable: <code id="env-var-747">QUARKUS_HTTP_AUTH_INCLUSIVE</code><button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-target="#env-var-747" title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
<div class="paragraph description-decoration">
<p><i class="fa fa-chevron-down"></i><span>Show more</span></p>
</div></div></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock">boolean</p></td>
<td class="tableblock halign-left valign-middle"><p class="tableblock"><code>false</code></p></td>
</tr>

<button class="btn-copy fa fa-clipboard inline-btn-copy" data-clipboard-action="copy" data-clipboard-text='quarkus.http.auth.inclusive-mode' title="Copy to clipboard" do-not-collapse="true"></button></p>
